- Being able to check off a habit multiple times in one day (for instance, for medicine that needs to be taken morning and night)
- Being able to duplicate already created habits so as not to have to set all parameters from scratch

reviews.text:
Another Broken Habit Tracker. I downloaded this after InnerGrow’s Habit Tracker app failed to accurately keep track of my completed habits. Onrise was free and had good privacy features, so I gave it a try. I used Onrise for two months and it was great. Then they released their monthly At a Glance feature. I completed all my habits for January, but according to this new feature I completed only 30 of 31 days. What’s the point of using a habit tracker app if it can’t even do the thing it supposed to do?

Reply to developer: Maybe I missed a day? I started using the app on December 8 and completed all goals. I also completed all goals for January, and the first day of February (the day I stopped using it). Your app said I had a 56-day streak (24 + 31 + 1). I wouldn’t have a 56-day streak if I missed a day, would I? Maybe you just missed a line in the code?

reviews.text:
Soooo great!. This app is so great! I love how simple, easy to use, and nice looking it is!
The one thing I would suggest is to look at the UI of the app "Atoms." and read Atomic Habits by james clear and try to implement some of the tips from that book in the app, like habit stacking.

Also regarding "Atoms." I think your UI could really really benefit from a satisfying animation when you click off a habit like in Atoms so its satisfying when you complete a habit. 

Also, I think it would be more helpful to see each habit in a list per-DAY instead of per-WEEK, and rhen have a weekly view of habits and if youve completed/failed throughout the week, instead of having that on the main habit checklist menu. That way #1 its easier to make it satisfying to complete the habit cause it can take up the whole card/screen, and #2 it makes it nicer for users cause you can see just that day instead of worrying about the whole week!

Free and Simple. In short: it does what I want and helps me feel good about achieving those small or big habits in a simple way so I don’t get full of myself.

Love it!. I just downloaded this app, and love it so far! I enjoy the simplicity of it and that it’s not trying to be 1000 things at once. The UI is intuitive and pleasant to look at and I only have a few suggestions on how it could be better. 

The habits tracker: I love how easy it is to add new habits and give them a minimum unit. However, I wish there was an option to see your count for habits that you plan to do twice or multiple times a day. For example, if I want to meditate twice a day as my goal, I can only mark the goal as done when I’ve done both rather than when I’ve done the first one. I’m asking for this feature because if I check it off as I go along my day, I’m more likely to stick with the routine. Whereas if I do something in the morning but have to wait until that night to mark it, I’m more likely to forget about it. 

The focus timer: I wish we could do custom times. I love the design of it and that it counts the total time and has cycles, but everyone pomodoros differently. Using the meditation example again, if I only want to do 10 minutes I either have to do 5 or 15. While it’s workable, it’s not ideal and I end up getting off the app and using something else

This is all I can think of for now but I am loving it so far!
